annotations.title: Create a Fun Friday custom pack

description: Create a custom content pack for the user's Fun Friday team, so the team plays their own material: Trivia Blitz questions (pack_type "trivia"), Imposter word lists (pack_type "faker") or Emoji Story phrases (pack_type "emoji_story"). A custom pack replaces the game's built-in content with the team's own — in-jokes, company trivia, a theme for the week. Only these three games take custom packs; for any other game, say so rather than calling this. Send the content in the one list that matches pack_type (for Imposter, either words or word_groups), and write it to play well (see each list's description). The host picks the pack in the lobby before pressing Start. Custom packs need a Pro or Business plan, which caps how many a team can keep — call funfriday_get_team first if unsure.

name.description: The pack's name as the team will see it in the lobby, e.g. "Office trivia". Up to 60 characters.

pack_type.description: Which game the pack is for: "trivia" (Trivia Blitz), "faker" (Imposter) or "emoji_story" (Emoji Story).

phrases.description: For pack_type "emoji_story" only: 1–500 phrases for players to tell in emoji — film titles, sayings, team in-jokes (up to 200 characters each). Choose phrases a player could tell with a handful of emoji and the room could guess; avoid abstract or very long ones.

questions.description: For pack_type "trivia" only: the questions, 100 at most. Each has text (up to 300 characters), exactly four options (up to 100 characters each) and correct_index, the 0-based index of the right option. Make the three wrong options plausible, keep options similar in length, and vary which position is correct. Ten to twenty questions makes a good game.

correct_index.description: Index (0–3) of the correct option in options.

explanation.description: Optional. One line on why the answer is right, shown to the room after the question closes (up to 300 characters). Worth adding for company or onboarding facts.

word_groups.description: For pack_type "faker" only, instead of words, when the pack covers several themes (a company pack with tools, meetings and snacks): up to 50 groups, each with a name and at least 2 words of the same kind. A round deals both of its words from one group, so the imposter's word is always a near miss ("Slack" against "Teams", never "Slack" against "Biscuits"). Four or more words per group plays best; 500 words at most across all groups.

name.description: What the group's words have in common, e.g. "Our tools". Up to 40 characters; players never see it.

words.description: At least two words or short phrases of the same kind.

For pack_type "faker" only, when every word belongs to ONE theme: 2–500 related words or short phrases (up to 100 characters each). Each round pairs any two of them — one for the group, a near miss for the imposter — so they must all be the same kind of thing. Pick words close enough that the imposter can bluff (e.g. "latte", "espresso", "cappuccino"), not opposites or unrelated words. Ten or more gives variety across rounds. If the pack covers more than one theme, send word_groups instead.
